title: Optimization for machine learning
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the optimization behind training models: gradients, Jacobians and Hessians, the multivariable chain rule, convex sets and functions, gradient descent and step sizes, convergence rates, stochastic gradient descent and mini-batches, momentum and adaptive methods, Newton's method, constrained optimization with Lagrange multipliers and the KKT conditions, duality, and the non-convex landscapes of deep learning.
primary_reading: Mathematics for Machine Learning by Deisenroth, Faisal and Ong (free PDF)

weeks.2: The multivariable chain rule in matrix form
weeks.4: Optimality conditions and why convexity matters
weeks.5: Gradient descent and the choice of step size
weeks.6: Convergence: smoothness, strong convexity and rates
weeks.9: Adaptive methods: AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam
weeks.11: Constrained optimization: Lagrange multipliers and the KKT conditions
weeks.12: Duality, and non-convex optimization: saddle points and local minima

blocks.deliverable: Derive the gradients of five common loss functions.
Prove or refute the convexity of six functions.
Run gradient descent with three step sizes and explain what happens.
Week 7 midterm; compare full-batch and stochastic descent on one problem.
Implement Adam and Newton steps on a test function.
Solve a constrained problem with Lagrange multipliers and check it numerically.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Optimizer study: implement gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent with momentum, Adam and Newton's method in plain Python, run them on a convex quadratic, a logistic regression problem and Rosenbrock's function, and write a report with convergence tables, the step sizes you tried, and an explanation of each result in terms of the theory.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
